about: Frozen judge rows (endstage-report.md 1d, tier 1): each row is a false clean Chrome measured, or a twin of one (review 4b-4c: `#unrelated`, `#sc9012-elsewhere` (a placeless code's too), `#sc9012-mount-line`, `#sc9012-prop-on-tag`, `#sc9012-enclosing`, `#sc9012-member-call-other-column`; `#sc9012-helper-call` and `#sc9012-member-call`, the covered controls); a judge or table change that answers otherwise fails judge-frozen.test.mjs. siteRows.note: A dependency function closing over a store: nothing says what its unread body writes, so the row at its argument is no answer.
Its twin: a standard function writes its first argument, so the row there is a gap.
Chrome frames each element of a pattern (probe3: `{ a, b } = st` at a and at b). A row at `a` says nothing about the read at `b`.
Its twin: the checker reports a pattern once, at its start, so that row covers each element.

an effect created in an effect's apply callback (census effect-apply): Solid throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK on line 7 and halts; missing-owner's V there is a stacked claim, its pair proved by patterns/stacked/s5-apply-context
the same halt with a V of a rule no twin proves: a false positive
a halted run whose V line ran with no code of its rule anywhere and none on it (smoke mx-dynamic-static-promise-flw-settled-report-error): a false positive
a halted run where the V's rule code is placed only on another line (smoke leaf-owner-forbidden-call in iife layers): a false positive
a halted run before the V's line ran: not-fired, never a false positive

Solid reports a store write once: the write at 5 is reported, the same `s1.v` write at 7 is not (census aw-shared-after-assign); the pair's twin patterns/stacked/r2-store-write-once proves it: a stacked claim
review of 1d6abdb80: the report at 5 writes `s1.v`, the finding at 7 `s1.w`; Solid reports per source, so the report confirms nothing at 7: a false positive
a strict read of `r1` at 5 reported, the same read at 7 not; Chrome reports a strict read per call (flw-owned-twice probe), so no twin proves the pair: a false positive
the rule's code was also reported with no authored line (census CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND then-named): it may be the finding's, so the row is an unjudged claim, listed, never cleared

the rule's code reported at 5, the finding's line 7 counted and never run (flw-mixed-dead: `if (Math.random() > 2) { h1(); }`, the call a V because a branch the checker cannot evaluate is reachable): unexecuted, so the row keeps its own outcome, never a false positive

a run that records PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK and SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC on the V's line (apply-placed-twin, R2h pa12): besideCode lists missing-owner for the first, so the row's own code is no reason to judge it
the same two codes with PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK on another line: nothing on the V's lines stands beside it
Chrome's frame for `r1.bind(null)()` sits on the `)`: the same bound read twice is a repeat, stacked/r1c-bind-read-twice
a bound read of another source is no repeat
`get()()` reads what `get` returned, `get()` reads `get`: the walk back to `(` must not make them one source
Review R14: the halting code's own rule has a finding in the file: no secondary
